statement: A taxi company's fare is a linear function of the distance traveled. The table shows the fares for two trips. $$\begin{array}{c|c} \text{Distance (miles)} & \text{Fare (dollars)} \\ \hline 3 & 11.10 \\ 8 & 22.60 \end{array}$$ What is the fare, in dollars, for a $12$-mile trip?

choices.misconception: I found the rate of $\$2.30$ per mile and multiplied it by $12$, leaving out the fixed starting charge of $\$4.20$.
I treated the fare as proportional to distance and used $22.60 \div 8 = 2.825$ dollars per mile for all $12$ miles.
I saw that $12$ miles is $4$ times $3$ miles, so I multiplied the $3$-mile fare of $\$11.10$ by $4$.

hints: Use the two rows to find the cost per mile.
The slope is the change in fare over the change in distance. Then use either row to find the starting charge.
The rate is $\frac{22.60 - 11.10}{8 - 3} = 2.30$ dollars per mile.

solutions.reliable: The rate is $\frac{22.60 - 11.10}{8 - 3} = \frac{11.50}{5} = 2.30$ dollars per mile. The starting charge is $11.10 - 3(2.30) = 4.20$ dollars, so the fare is $F = 4.20 + 2.30d$. For $12$ miles, $F = 4.20 + 27.60 = 31.80$ dollars.
solutions.elegant: From $8$ miles to $12$ miles is $4$ more miles at $\$2.30$ each, so the fare is $22.60 + 4(2.30) = 31.80$ dollars.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
